ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:9:`ThreadCtx` is a 1,408-byte object, with a one-byte atomic `Role` (`Idle=0`, `Ifid=1`, `Ex=2`), a separately published ready role, the active wake endpoint, client/shard pointer vectors, command counters, signals, and inbound transports. The maximum is 128 physical server threads. `Ifid` is the implementation's name for the combined receive/parse/dispatch/send role; there is no separate sender role (`src/core/thread.h:57`, `:303`, `:1131`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:14:| `1s` / `fused` | Every thread runs `IoLoop` with an `ExLoopT<true>` driven inside it. Both placement vectors (`ifid_threads`, `ex_threads`) contain every thread; the stored role is still `Ifid`. The IO loop owns the blocking wait and published wake endpoint. | The ordinary route still posts to the shard owner's task lane, including the self lane. Same-thread completion can call the IO completion callback directly. The optional local-read lane adds foreign-store reads under separate lifetime and ordering checks. |
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:16:The mode boundary is a boot-time template choice, not a branch that turns each command into a different kind of executor. Split allocates both loop arrays in `src/main.cc:336`, provisions the opposite role before serving (`:387`, `:521`), and selects the loop at `:424` and `:560`. Fused does the analogous allocation at `src/core/genthread.cc:88`, initializes on the pinned thread at `:122`, binds the executor into IO at `:165`, and starts serving only after the loaded/ready/running boot barrier. `Placement::build_fused` rewrites role labels to `Ifid` and duplicates the two thread views (`src/core/placement.h:37`). Fusion therefore changes scheduling and handoffs; it preserves single-owner writes.
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:20:Without explicit placement or ratio, split requests every allowed CPU, with `io = N - floor(N/2)` and `ex = floor(N/2)`; fused selects every allowed CPU for both duties. Placement rejects a total above 128 rather than resizing the channel mesh. The default 16 shards are assigned round-robin over executor thread IDs; accepted shard counts are 1–256. A physical executor-capable thread can own zero shards (`src/core/server.h:238`, `:364`, `src/core/placement.h:37`, `:73`, `src/core/config.h:1266`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:37:`ExLoopT` contains its own 1,024-entry control/persistence ring, cached time/configuration, cursors for expiry and version cleanup, and six task/release debt queues: `atomic_deferred_`, `multi_retries_`, `xshard_retries_`, `ordered_deferred_`, `stale_tasks_`, and `stale_releases_`. Its `WbEngine` remains allocated for statistics but never serves clients. Split `ExLoop` is locked to 6,112 bytes (`src/core/ex_loop.h:181`, `:213`, `:3327`, `:3369`, `:3425`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:39:An ordinary split pass services stale forwards and borrow returns first, then MULTI retries, atomic deferrals, and scatter retries. Fresh tasks wait while scatter retry debt or ordered deferrals remain. After execution it flushes pending group decisions, services blocking waiters on a 10 ms beat, and advances persistence/control work. A pass with no work counts as idle, spins with `pause` for a 2,048-pass budget, then performs an unmasked sweep and arms a kernel wait. Once a placement drain has been acknowledged, even expiry and config refresh must stop touching the shard vector (`src/core/ex_loop.h:701`, `:731`, `:759`, `:769`, `:800`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:49:The other three transport families retain one fixed 1,024-slot channel per producer: completed-client notices, `(shard, pointer)` borrow returns, and IO-to-IO `ClientTransfer` records. A task push publishes initialized bytes with a release tail store; ordinary SPSC publication needs no contended producer RMW. The notification mask does use atomic operations, amortized by batching. Ordinary dispatch leaves the frame at the parse cursor when enqueue fails, so it can be parsed again after capacity returns; scatter reserves its whole fanout before publication (`src/core/thread.h:96`, `:110`, `src/exec/exqueue.h:30`, `src/core/io_loop.h:5246`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:51:Masks select active producers; they are not the only correctness witness. The 100 µs signal sweep republishes task bits for nonempty lanes, and the pre-park path scans channels without the mask. Parking publishes blocked state and executes a sequentially consistent fence before checking inbound work. A producer wakes only on the relevant transition while the consumer is blocked. Prepared wake SQEs are submitted before another busy iteration; otherwise a queued wake could remain outside the kernel indefinitely (`src/core/thread.h:854`, `:896`, `:1006`, `:1088`, `src/core/io_loop.h:686`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:53:Runtime SIGINT/SIGTERM sets `Server::shutting_down_`, sets each published thread's stop flag, and rings the shutdown doorbell. These are outer-loop stop conditions, separate from placement-drain acknowledgements. The epoll park has a 50 ms ceiling so an idle loop rechecks stop even without a new connection. Main joins workers before releasing store-held MVCC references and reaping IO's deferred arenas; that final single-threaded lifetime cleanup must precede IO-pool destruction (`src/main.cc:63`, `:351`, `:594`, `src/core/ex_loop.h:705`, `src/core/io_loop.h:547`, `:724`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:65:A command-wide group is an arena-resident `ScatterState`, not a `ShardGroup`. `ShardGroup` is only one touched shard's range in `key_order[]`. `ScatterState` owns the shared pending count, references, command kind, phase, origin connection, snapshot/expiry cuts, gathered results, and one isolated 64-byte decision line containing `atomic<uint64_t> epoch` and `atomic<bool> aborted`. Epoch zero means undecided/private; a nonzero epoch is a commit ticket. An aborted epoch-zero entry is decided-aborted, not unfinished. Ordinary pseudo-entries carry their own plain `epoch`; EXEC entries can have `group==nullptr` while still pointing to a transaction's shared decision (`src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:80`, `:429`, `:590`, `src/store/atomic_mvcc.h:24`, `src/store/flatstore_atomic.inc:524`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:79:### Drawing a ticket is not publishing a readable cut
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:81:`Server::commit_seq_` is a 64-bit ticket dispenser. `atomic_commit_safe_` is the separately published read watermark. A commit batch increments `atomic_commit_inflight_`, reserves consecutive tickets with one `commit_seq_.fetch_add`, release-stores tickets into all its decision words, then loads the drawn sequence **before** decrementing the inflight count. Only the decrement that observes one outstanding committer can CAS the safe watermark upward to that sampled sequence. If another committer is still between reservation and epoch publication, the safe watermark stays behind (`src/core/server.h:2560`, `:2576`, `:2587`, `:2619`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:83:There is no admission-order commit frontier. Install order and ticket order can differ. Successful standalone groups whose last owner has finished are linked into a thread-local intrusive commit list without allocating. At the executor boundary, one reserve/publish bracket assigns consecutive tickets to the list, then completes AOF/notification work, closes each apply window, release-stores `OpState::Done`, and notifies IO. The “last owner publishes” description therefore includes a delay until that owner's commit-batch flush (`src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:3718`, `:3790`, `:3815`). Same-owner `atomic_commit()` closes its bracket before installing its local records; its justification is that no other task can run on those owned shards before the current task returns (`src/core/server.h:2610`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:85:### A read cut pins a representation, not the reply
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:87:`SnapshotCut` contains the inclusive 64-bit cut, slot index, registration bit, and atomic completion bit. Exactly one `ScatterArenaPool` per IO writes that IO's `Server::atomic_read_floors_` slot. It maintains a vector of unresolved cuts and a cached exact minimum/count. It publishes **cut + 1**, with `UINT64_MAX` meaning no constraint, then reloads the safe watermark and adopts a newer confirmed cut if publication raced a commit. This is one publish/confirm adjustment, not a retry-until-stable reader loop (`src/cmd/xshard.h:76`, `src/cmd/atomics_glue.inc:324`, `:349`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:89:Cleanup loads the safe commit cutoff first and the global minimum floor second. A prefix entry is eligible when aborted, or when its epoch is nonzero, strictly below the floor, and no greater than the earlier cutoff. The sequentially consistent registration/cutoff/floor operations make a cleanup that misses a new registration use an older cutoff. A physical snapshot freezes collapse entirely (`src/core/ex_loop.h:2022`, `src/core/server.h:2735`, `src/store/flatstore_atomic.inc:1491`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:91:At the last result-producing fragment, the command marks its cut complete and increments the IO completion counter. IO removes completed cuts before ordered reply retirement, so a slow earlier reply does not pin versions that no fragment will read again. Gathered borrowed values have their own borrow lifetime. Removing the last minimum rescans the unresolved vector; ordinary removals use swap/pop and update the moved slot (`src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:3712`, `src/cmd/atomics_glue.inc:401`, `:430`). The usual unresolved-cut admission limit is **eight per IO**, enforced while atomic activity is present; read-only gaps can carry more, bounded by the participating ROBs. Cross-owner scripts use their own cut limit. A full window returns backpressure before posting (`src/cmd/xshard.h:117`, `src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:1822`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:99:Each owner updates its own cache-line-separated `OwnerRecordRefs::nodes`; only its final node release decrements the shared state reference. A completion sentinel prevents an early-aborted entry from releasing the state before that owner's final task. `AtomicEntry::owner_refs` is a raw pointer into this owner-indexed array. Migration does not transfer that reference accounting; §5 describes the resulting shared-counter defect (`src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:416`, `src/store/atomic_mvcc.h:28`). Reply retirement returns the admission credit and frees unneeded result contents; the arena itself stays until both record and WATCH references reach zero. Failure to allocate deferred-destruction bookkeeping intentionally leaks that arena rather than freeing live decision pointers (`src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:3997`, `src/cmd/atomics_glue.inc:467`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:101:Entries are recycled by allocation class up to 4,096 cached entries and 4 MiB per store. Armed read-local objects additionally wait for their QSBR grace period before reuse; wire borrows can retain them beyond that. At shutdown, after workers join, fused first drains every local-read retirement FIFO and disables all stores' retirement hooks. Then every remaining epoch-zero group is marked aborted, collapse runs with unlimited cut/floor, and store-held group references are dropped before IO arena pools disappear. Disarming the hooks first prevents this unbounded final collapse from filling a FIFO whose readers can no longer publish another grace period (`src/store/flatstore_atomic.inc:927`, `:2269`, `src/core/genthread.cc:100`, `src/main.cc:352`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:105:`--atomic-window -1` resolves at boot to `min(16 * shards, 1024)`; zero is unlimited. Credits count admitted write groups through reply retirement, not installed records or commit tickets. `AtomicAdmissionLease` occupies a separate 64-byte-aligned thread-context block: IO privately owns `generation`, `available`, and `active`, and publishes `published_active` for CONFIG/INFO (`src/core/config.h:349`, `src/core/server.h:195`, `src/core/thread.h:65`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:107:Admission rejects a snapshot barrier or an odd credit generation, CAS-borrows up to **eight** credits from the shared pool if its private lease is empty, consumes one available credit, publishes active count, and rechecks mode/generation/barrier. A race rolls back admission. Exhaustion leaves the request pending before fanout. Returning the last active group also returns the unused lease batch so an idle IO does not keep credits from an active peer (`src/core/server.h:2449`, `:2460`, `:2517`, `:3210`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:109:CONFIG reconfiguration CASes the generation odd, waits for announced pool mutations, snapshots every IO's published active count into `reconfig_carry`, sets pool to `max(window-active,0)` and debt to `max(active-window,0)`, then publishes the next even generation. Old unused leases are discarded. Retiring an old-generation group pays debt before replenishing the pool; credit release spins while reconfiguration is odd. Turning atomic mode off stops optional new groups but existing activity and version lists remain live until drained (`src/core/server.h:2434`, `:3287`, `:3319`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:111:`apply_open` is a second, shorter lifetime: admission through the all-owner decision/abort edge. Physical snapshot coordination waits on this apply count, not admission leases, because an IO blocked inside SAVE cannot retire the replies that would return its leases. Confusing these counters creates a circular wait (`src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:480`, `src/core/server.h:2772`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:115:`MultiSession` is connection-owned, allocated on demand, and stores copied argv strings, queue-error state, watched keys, and a prepared-but-unpublished EXEC. At EXEC, IO force-admits one group even with `atomic=0`, constructs `MultiExecState`, and lowers commands into per-shard ordered command-index lists with one cursor per shard. Each child has its own `Op`, completion counter, stage, per-shard done markers, and optional scatter state. The outer transport is a normal 32-byte `Task` whose scatter pointer has low bit one to tag `MultiExecState` (`src/cmd/multi.inc:8`, `:45`, `:101`, `:123`, `:1427`, `:1827`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:117:IO proves room for every outer shard task before publishing any. A full task lane or read-cut window retains the prepared EXEC and sets connection backpressure. It initializes owner-reference sentinels only on the final publication path, since a prepared request can outlive a shard migration. `exec_read_fanout` registers one shared cut through the **outer IO's** scatter pool when the transaction contains cross-shard MGET/EXISTS, a read scatter child with more than one shard group, or dereferencing SORT (including STORE). Its child pool must not overwrite that IO's floor. Other transactions register no MVCC cut. This test counts shards, despite its “multi-owner” comment; even several separate one-key reads in one EXEC do not themselves arm a shared cut. Every transaction nevertheless stamps one expiry clock, shared by all children (`src/cmd/multi.inc:664`, `:1551`, `:1574`, `:1627`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:121:Every fragment first joins the WATCH phase. Each watched key is validated/reserved on its owner under the transaction time cut; dirty WATCH state sets `watch_failed` and aborts execution. No command list proceeds until `watch_pending` reaches zero. Owner-side `watchers_` and `watch_reservations_` maps live inside `Shard`; reservation records retain the decision word and lifetime pin, so they remain meaningful when a group has installed no version (`src/core/shard.h:244`, `:493`, `src/cmd/multi.inc:1203`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:125:**Two WATCH-validating EXECs can still form a wait cycle.** Let two connections WATCH `a,b` on different owners, then both EXEC read-only bodies. If owner A first validates transaction T and owner B first validates U, each installs its own blocking reservation. T's validation on B and U's validation on A both stop at `watch_finalize_reservation` before the nonblocking-mutator abort rule. Neither can finish the all-shard WATCH barrier, hence neither can decide/release the reservation the other needs. `service_multi_retries` keeps retrying without a validation timeout or priority rule. This path needs no intervening write or expiry (`src/cmd/multi.inc:1203`, `:2176`, `:2261`, `src/core/ex_loop.h:3025`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:127:Each shard advances only its own command-list cursor. A child touching several shards uses a command barrier; an owner that has done its stage returns `Retry` until the child finishes or publishes a new stage. Cross-shard child membership is captured into **four stages of four 64-bit masks**, covering 256 shards; the last old-stage participant rebuilds groups, writes the new immutable membership mask, then release-stores `stage`. Barrier-only fragments read that published mask, not the mutable scatter table (`src/cmd/multi.inc:45`, `:1911`, `:1959`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:133:After finishing its list, each shard emits its AOF fragment once and decrements `lists_pending`. The final list claims `finalizer_claimed` by CAS. Success draws one ticket, publishes it to the parent and all child scatter epoch words inside the same safe-watermark bracket, and release-stores `finalized`. A child runtime error retains its own abort flag, so other queued commands can commit; a queue error gives EXECABORT, and a transaction-level failure aborts every child. Every outer task then finalizes reservations and releases its owner sentinel. The final `tasks_pending` decrement permits the public EXEC operation to become Done. IO assembles the command-order reply and returns the admission credit; state destruction still waits for retained version/WATCH references (`src/cmd/multi.inc:1289`, `:1997`, `:2035`, `:2048`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:137:EVAL/FCALL with keys in multiple shards use another `ScatterState` phase machine even when `--atomic 0`. Zero/one-key and same-shard activations take the local route; disabling any of the stage-byte, workbench-byte, or cut-slot facilities retains the legacy route and its refusal when declared keys need different owners. The enabled scatter decision distinguishes shards, so two shards on one physical executor still use these waves (`src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:1460`, `:1742`, `:1836`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:139:`Pin` installs an exact-key `AtomicScriptIntent` on every declared key, including absent keys: a malloc'd header plus copied key bytes on the store's singly linked intent list, with a 32-bit reference count for overlapping activations. No value/version is installed by a pin. Instead, `atomic_needs_version` and `begin_plain_version` force subsequent ordinary writes on that key to preserve their predecessor and draw a ticket. After all pins complete, the final participant chooses `script_cut = atomic_snapshot()`. `Read` serializes each declared value at that cut and the command's common expiry time into `ObjectImage` arrays. This costs a serialization and payload allocation per staged value, plus one relaxed shared byte-counter addition per fragment (`src/store/flatstore_atomic.inc:82`, `:129`, `src/cmd/atomics_glue.inc:10`, `src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:2422`, `:3440`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:141:`Run` posts one task to the current owner of the first key's coordinator shard. That thread lazily retains a private `Shard` in `thread_local ScriptWorkbench`, outside `Server::shards()`. Each attempt clears its table, loads all staged images, executes the Lua handler synchronously, and serializes written keys into `state.apply`. One byte per declared key records read bit 1 and successful-write bit 2; Validate selects the read set, Apply the write set. A Lua command error does not erase earlier successful nested writes: the handler's reply and recorded write set both survive into Apply. The private store's object-byte limit is checked after loading and after Lua returns, so it is not a peak-allocation cap during Lua. Real-shard hit/miss statistics receive the private workbench's deltas (`src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:2278`, `:2381`, `:2474`, `src/cmd/scripting.cc:394`, `:634`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:143:A read-only activation skips certification and tickets, unpins, and finishes at its read cut. A writing activation CAS-acquires the server-wide `script_certification_active_`, reserves an unpublished commit ticket, and posts Validate. This global flag serializes scripts' certification-through-Apply even for disjoint keys; ordinary writers never acquire it. Validation scans matching MVCC records and rejects any non-aborted epoch-zero record or committed epoch greater than `script_cut`. Losing certification or finding a conflict discards the reply/images/notification batch, advances the cut, and reruns Read/Run with pins still held. The default retry allowance is eight, giving at most nine attempts; exhaustion returns `TRYAGAIN Cross-shard script conflicted, retry` after unpinning (`src/core/server.h:210`, `:2721`, `src/store/flatstore_atomic.inc:155`, `src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:3496`, `:3516`, `:3543`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:145:After successful validation, the implementation posts **Unpin before Apply**. Unpin decrements/frees the intents and rebuilds the group arrays; Apply initializes owner record references, installs the written images through ordinary atomic image-apply, then the final owner release-stores the reserved ticket into `state.epoch`, publishes the safe watermark, releases certification, and completes AOF/notification work. Every wave preflights all destination channels. A full channel retries publication without exposing a partial wave; `pending = task_completions + 1` includes a poster reference so a peer cannot rebuild the shared group arrays while the posting loop still uses them. Engine OOM aborts the group and closes any reserved ticket/certification state. Script cut-window exhaustion returns BUSY immediately, whereas ordinary atomic-credit exhaustion returns dispatch backpressure (`src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:1822`, `:2289`, `:2337`, `:3410`, `:3569`, `:3596`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:147:**This phase order leaves a lost-update window.** Let a script stage `a=0`, run `INCR a` privately, and pass Validate; choose another declared key on a second shard so it uses scatter. After Unpin on `a` and before Apply on `a`, another connection's ordinary `INCR a` can read physical zero, write one, and reply one. With no earlier record or other pin on `a`, that write takes the unversioned path. Script Apply then installs its computed one, and the script also replies one. Final `a=1` cannot serialize two successful increments. Apply performs no script read-set revalidation, and the script certification flag excludes no plain writer. The comment that the reserved ticket orders every later writer after the activation does not cover a writer that observed the pre-activation value; after Unpin, that writer need not draw a ticket at all (`src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:2526`, `:2538`, `:3569`, `src/cmd/atomics_glue.inc:122`, `:966`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:149:Auto stage budget is 4 MiB without maxmemory, otherwise `clamp(maxmemory / shards / 16, 4 MiB, 64 MiB)`; workbench budget is twice that and cut slots default to four per IO pool. Staging checks the sum of `sizeof(ObjectImage) + key length + payload bytes` after each owner serializes its fragment, so that cap is also checked after allocation. `script-crossshard-conflict-retries 0` allows the first attempt and disables retries; unlike the other three zero-valued knobs, it does **not** disable the facility. Lua's separate default instruction limit is 100,000, counted by a hook every 1,000 VM instructions; the hook fails on `instructions > limit`, so exact multiples get one extra hook interval. Zero maps to `UINT64_MAX`. The hook does not bound time spent inside a nested C++ command (`src/core/server.h:202`, `src/core/config.h:369`, `src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:2464`, `src/cmd/scripting.cc:329`, `:1087`, `:1343`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:155:Only GET/MGET are local candidates. Active MULTI/WATCH, blocked/subscriber state, conservative routes, pending own writes, and earlier owner operations can force the owner path. MGET also refuses key-miss notification mode. A GET miss goes to the owner; a stable MGET miss contributes nil locally. Typed or expiry-due objects demote the whole read so the owner performs the required lookup/expiry effects. Local replies copy bytes before the thread publishes quiescence; they do not retain a foreign raw pointer for the send (`src/core/io_loop.h:4398`, `src/core/ex_loop.h:1205`, `:1488`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:163:### Foreign visibility uses both a filter and sequence validation
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:165:The extended `ReadLocalStoreState` includes a 64-bit `probe_sequence`, owner mutation nesting/pending counts, retirement sink, and `ForeignReadSafety`. Sequence bit 0 means table mutation in progress; bit 1 is the pending hint; bits 2–63 are a generation. Closing the outer mutation bracket increments the generation; saturation permanently refuses local reads. Table resize/movement and atomic physical exchanges change this sequence; an ordinary immutable one-slot SET does not (`src/store/flatstore.h:555`, `:626`, `:3494`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:167:The foreign filter is **4,096 64-bit cells plus 4,096 32-bit touch epochs** per armed shard, not an exact key map. Each cell packs a 31-bit count, 32-bit fingerprint, and wildcard bit. A second fingerprint sharing an occupied cell makes it wildcard until the cell drains. Count saturation keeps it positive until a complete drain can rebuild; unenumerable mutations add one wildcard reference to every cell, and bookkeeping overflow poisons permanently. Owners publish a cell before advancing its epoch; readers acquire-load it. Prepared atomic entries publish the complete unsafe key span before physical changes and close it only when raw visibility is safe again (`src/store/foreign_read_safety.h:22`, `:65`, `:94`, `:195`, `src/store/flatstore_atomic.inc:1241`). “Exact per-key filter” in configuration comments overstates this mechanism.
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:169:A point probe samples the sequence, rejects a positive key filter or an odd/poisoned sequence, acquire-loads both table pointer/capacity/mask triples, and **rechecks the sequence before indexing**. It probes slots with acquire loads and compares full key bytes, then checks the sequence again. After copying the payload, `read_local_validate` checks it yet again. Pending-bit changes alone are ignored by the sequence comparison. With prefetch capture enabled, the exact key-verified object survives from prefetch to execute; execution does not reload a newer slot (`src/store/flatstore.h:914`, `:942`, `:3348`, `src/core/ex_loop.h:1502`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:171:MGET surrounds every value load/copy with a command-wide window. Up to 128 keys and with the atomic filter enabled, it records/rechecks per-key cell epochs; otherwise it records/rechecks touched-shard generations. It builds a private reply and clears it on a failed window. **Both MGET implementations make up to two attempts.** The noncaptured GET path makes up to three probe/copy attempts; default captured GET breaks on a topology/validation failure instead of recapturing. Failure then demotes to owner execution. These are per-operation sequence checks and reader retries in the default build of an enabled local-read lane; they conflict with the supplied “no reader retries and no seqlocks” law (`src/core/ex_loop.h:1015`, `:1028`, `:1054`, `:1170`, `:1299`, `:1450`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:175:The read-local grace epoch is separate from the MVCC commit epoch. `ReadLocalThreadState::tick` publishes a rotation's quiescence with bit 63 denoting parked. The epoch and park/resume publications are sequentially consistent. Resuming first removes parked status while retaining the conservative old tick, then republishes the current epoch before probing. Grace scans ignore parked threads and require every active tick to be **strictly greater** than the retirement stamp; a remembered blocking participant is checked first (`src/core/thread.h:922`, `src/core/server.h:586`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:179:A full retirement ring makes the writer publish its own quiescence, repeatedly drain, execute `pause`, and call `sched_yield()` until a slot frees. There is no deadline or overflow allocation. A stalled active reader can therefore hold this owner inside reclamation indefinitely; in fused mode that physical thread also services connections. This is an explicit boundary to any unconditional non-obstruction claim (`src/core/read_local.h:299`, `:416`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:183:The source-default SET representation remains immutable while this lane is armed. However, `TOMO_READ_LOCAL_SET_TAX_VARIANT=1` and `=3` are accepted build selectors for shard-sequence and per-object-sequence **in-place** overwrite. Selector 3 overlays a 32-bit raw-object sequence into the header and atomically copies mutable payload cells; sequence exhaustion falls back to replacement. Selector 2 is rejected because post-grace recycling became unconditional. The accepted overwrite builds explicitly violate the supplied in-place/sequence laws (`src/store/read_local_settax.h:17`, `src/store/kvobj.h:74`, `src/store/flatstore.h:2771`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:187:### Preparing and publishing the first wave
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:191:The shortcut named `same_owner` compares **shard IDs**, not physical owner IDs. Ordinary eligible commands whose keys all hit one shard become an ordinary local command. Different shards on the same executor still produce separate tasks and a scatter arena. Forced atomic children, dereferencing SORT, and selected command-specific cases bypass the shortcut. Read-fanout cut selection likewise uses more than one shard group, not more than one physical owner (`src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:1742`, `:1798`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:193:Each participating shard gets one 32-byte `Task`, naming the same public ROB operation and `ScatterState` but a different explicit shard. IO counts the required slots in every destination owner's producer lane **before publishing any task**. Insufficient capacity destroys the unpublished preparation, leaves the input frame unconsumed, and retries later. Atomic waves publish each owner's shard tasks under one tail update, and preinitialize that owner's record sentinel before exposing any task. This saves tail publications; it does not collapse the tasks into one executor-major job (`src/core/io_loop.h:5009`, `:5063`, `:5107`, `src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:1090`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:201:Two-hop image commands first gather source objects into `ObjectImage` values, using type-specific snapshot serialization, including TTL and collection encoding. The last completing executor combines the images, builds destination groups, and posts the next wave **directly to executor task lanes**. SORT with actual BY/GET dereferences adds a source-image wave and a derived-key gather wave before possible store work. The ordinary two-hop/all-shard path requires the connection's older ROB operations to drain before publication and arms a parser barrier against younger work; one-wave MGET/MSET and the direct atomic rename path do not take that barrier (`src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:282`, `:1216`, `:1264`, `:1872`, `:3675`, `src/core/io_loop.h:4990`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:205:Successful standalone atomic install/apply finalizers enter the executor's intrusive commit queue. The executor flush assigns ordered tickets and release-publishes group decisions, closes the apply lifetime, sets the public operation `Done`, and notifies its connection owner. Failed groups publish abort and finish without a successful epoch. Read cuts can complete as soon as the last future value dereference finishes, independently of when the public reply reaches the ROB head (`src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:3711`, `:3743`, `:3790`, `:3815`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:213:`Rob<64>` is the connection's reply-order mechanism. It can hold 64 issued operations and lazily allocates eight-operation chunks: 2,688 bytes per chunk, at most 21,504 bytes of `Op` storage beyond the 192-byte ROB header. Execution may set later slots `Done` first. `drain` acquire-loads from `flush` and stops at the first slot that is not `Done`, retires its reply and scatter state in sequence, then advances the released flush frontier. Completion notices are hints to inspect this ordered frontier, not permission to emit a later reply. `at(id)` only masks the slot number; it performs no generation check (`src/net/rob.h:140`, `:215`, `:737`, `:761`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:215:Borrow releases carry `(shard, pointer)` over their separate return channel and are forwarded if their remembered owner is stale. A full release channel keeps the release on IO's retry side; it cannot free the payload early. Scatter arenas can outlive reply retirement through atomic-record or WATCH references. Teardown first releases still-owned borrows, unregisters cuts, closes admission and script state, and defers arena destruction while references remain; the pool's allocation-failure fallback preserves lifetime by leaking rather than freeing a referenced arena (`src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:2052`, `:3997`, `src/cmd/atomics_glue.inc:467`, `src/core/ex_loop.h:3143`, `src/core/io_loop.h:5528`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:220:`Router` has 16,384 atomic 32-bit bucket words, each packing a 16-bit physical shard ID and 16-bit executor ID. Boot divides buckets into fixed contiguous shard ranges; any remainder belongs to the final shard. Runtime changes only owner bits. A shard's tables, objects, expiry state, borrow registry, MVCC list, WATCH maps, and AOF producer stay in the same `Shard`/`FlatStore` allocation. A transfer changes which thread may mutate them, not their addresses or physical memory residence (`src/core/shard.h:548`, `:567`, `:658`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:222:The range API accepts only one or more **whole stores**. A partial shard range is rejected even though routing names individual buckets. It validates ownership and vector membership and reserves destination vector capacity before acquiring `Router::transfer_writer_`. `begin_transfer` is a try-lock: an existing writer, non-idle phase, invalid range, or wrong source rejects the move. Successful begin records range/source/destination and release-publishes `Preparing`, while bucket routes still name the source (`src/core/server.h:1997`, `src/core/shard.h:606`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:226:Runtime requests never read the transfer descriptor. They can enqueue against an old route. Before **any** shard access, including tagged EXEC and ownerless cleanup, `ExLoop::execute` compares the current `worker_of_shard` with its physical thread. A mismatch forwards the original task; channel refusal stores it in `stale_tasks_`. Borrow releases use the same rule and their own `stale_releases_`. FIFO retry stops at the first full destination and rechecks ownership on every attempt. The protocol pays an extra task handoff for a stale route instead of a per-request routing epoch/retry (`src/core/ex_loop.h:2777`, `:3115`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:230:`flip_quiesced` requires empty task/release inbound frontiers, stale queues, atomic/EXEC/scatter retry queues, ordered-deferred queues, pending commit/notify work, and snapshot backlogs; no active snapshot owner; zero global admission leases and apply windows; and no shard notification or recording-AOF output pending. Fused read-local additionally requires an empty local lane and **empty QSBR retirement ring**. Once acknowledged, frozen loops stop task, expiry, cleanup, waiter, and config walks until the controller releases the stage (`src/core/ex_loop.h:1794`, `:509`, `:731`, `:800`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:234:**Retained MVCC owner-reference counters do not satisfy that ownership rule.** `AtomicEntry::owner_refs` points to the original `ScatterState::owner_record_refs[executor_slot].nodes` or EXEC equivalent, a plain `uint32_t` shared by that owner's records across shards. The quiescence predicate checks admission/apply lifetimes, not `atomic_has_records()`, and frozen passes do not force record collapse. A decided group can retire its reply and leave records in two shards on one owner; moving just one shard preserves both pointers to the same counter. Subsequent cleanup on the old and new owners both execute `--*entry->owner_refs` without synchronization. Neither transfer function rewrites these pointers or splits their counts. This is a concrete data-race path across the ownership edge, affecting the shared group lifetime pin; zero admission does not prove zero retained records (`src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:1090`, `:2673`, `src/cmd/multi.inc:934`, `src/store/flatstore_atomic.inc:1572`, `src/core/server.h:2765`, `src/core/ex_loop.h:1794`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:244:The destination reserves client/active/catalog/pubsub/tracking capacity and a writeback slot. The source reserves migration and forwarding records, removes the client from active/prepared work, and cancels the old io_uring receive; ownership remains at source until the kernel no longer holds the receive buffer. SQ starvation retries cancellation. Epoll instead duplicates the socket with `F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC`, reserves source rollback and destination registrations, and removes the original source registration. Before commit, failure restores catalog/routing state and re-arms source receive (`src/core/io_loop.h:322`, `:2545`, `:2575`, `:2750`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:246:Commit extracts the local catalog and pubsub/tracking routing, releases the source writeback slot, installs the `kWbMigrationInstalling` sentinel, removes source membership, updates the ROB's read-local statistics pointer, and publishes `Client::ifid_thread = destination` as the connection ownership edge. It updates the client directory and posts `ClientTransfer {client, catalog, routing, source}`. Destination drains this inbox before routed pubsub events, installs the reserved state and new writeback slot, and arms receive. A post failure after reserved capacity is an invariant abort, not a rollback across an ambiguous owner edge (`src/core/io_loop.h:2686`, `:2780`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:254:An executor keeps one countdown across visited keys. Every 64th visit increments the physical shard's bucket sample counter; a completed scatter fragment enumerates its touched hashes, so this measures key visits rather than commands or measured command service time. The controller folds unsigned 32-bit sample deltas multiplied by the sample rate into per-bucket EWMA weights, `new = 0.25 * sample + 0.75 * old`, with the first fold using the sample directly. Histories belong to immutable bucket IDs and survive migration. Every 10 ms an owner advances one owned shard's byte census by a 64-unit scan budget; byte totals are therefore asynchronous table-census observations, not instantaneous allocation counts (`src/core/ex_loop.h:2912`, `:3009`, `src/core/server.h:472`, `src/core/shard.h:337`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:256:Once per second, each IO enumerates its live clients and publishes `(connection ID, ROB dispatch ID, current in-flight depth)`. A client's new weight sample is `max(dispatch delta, in-flight depth)`; it uses the same 0.25 EWMA and is keyed by stable connection ID. The first observation includes all dispatches since that connection's zero baseline. The shared signal map is protected by `lb_signal_mu_`; owner totals are published as integer weights scaled by 1,024. Closed clients are erased. This signal does not measure socket bytes, TLS CPU, or parsing nanoseconds (`src/core/io_loop.h:7108`, `src/core/server.h:438`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:258:The fold also computes per-thread occupancy from busy/idle counter deltas, with the same EWMA. Continuous move selection below uses item weights and bytes, not that occupancy; flip's candidate selection can consult it. With controls disabled, per-request sampling is gated off and the corresponding signal arrays are not provisioned at boot (`src/core/server.h:492`, `src/core/ex_loop.h:186`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:266:For every unpinned item and every other destination, `weighted_lb_best_incremental_move` simulates moving its weight, bytes, and count. When demand is hot, a candidate must reduce demand span by more than `1e-9`; byte span is not a hard constraint. For a byte-only move, demand may increase by at most `1e-9` and byte span must fall by more than `1e-9`. Eligible candidates minimize resulting demand span, then byte span, then item-count span, then item ID and destination ID. **Continuous LB does not enforce equal shard/client counts**; count is a tie-breaker (`src/core/weighted_lb.h:50`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:268:The shard planner repeats this calculation up to `lb_move_cap`, updates its simulated loads, pins each chosen item, and stops once neither ratio is hot or no improving move exists. Any bucket still within its 5-second cooldown pins its whole shard. Client planning performs the same demand-only search once, yielding at most **one client per transaction regardless of move cap**. If both plans exist, the controller alternates preference. It consumes the chosen side's streak before starting the move (`src/core/server.h:1190`, `:1228`, `:1264`, `:1315`, `:1337`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:272:`shape_transition_mu_` serializes admission against flip, snapshots, and loading. The planner checks that state before folding and again before publishing; an active LB transaction or flip/snapshot/load refuses the beat. Allocation failure increments capacity refusal. On admission it clears acknowledgements, increments the LB epoch, sets a 5-second deadline, and publishes either `ExDrain` for a shard plan or `ClientDrain` for one client (`src/core/server.h:1111`, `:1317`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:276:Client balancing asks only the destination to reserve one slot, then the source waits for the chosen client to become movable. TLS, blocked state, or a MULTI-session pointer causes explicit refusal; ordinary live work can drain until timeout. `ClientMoving` begins before asynchronous receive cancellation and marks the cooldown immediately. Refusal and cancellation also consume cooldown, preventing repeatedly selecting an immovable heavy client. A 5-second timeout releases `ClientDrain`/`ExDrain`, but **does not cancel `ClientMoving`**: that phase remains until the asynchronous transfer commits or cancels. Wake SQ starvation retries the exact peer (`src/core/io_loop.h:2934`, `src/core/server.h:1395`, `:1444`, `src/core/ex_loop.h:1873`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:278:The full partitioner used by flip shares the weight/byte ordering but has a different invariant: each final target receives floor/ceil item count. It places pinned items first, sorts remaining items by descending demand, then bytes, then ID, and greedily selects least-loaded eligible targets with count/current-owner/ID tie-breaks. When the complete incumbent assignment satisfies count bounds and is no worse in both spans, it keeps it wholesale. This global incumbent check prevents a count-balanced no-op flip from reshuffling zero-weight items (`src/core/weighted_lb.h:131`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:284:Automatic flip is split-only and defaults off. `Server` owns one `FlipController`, written by the main monitor under its cold mutex. Its phases are `Disabled`, `BootPending`, `Measuring`, `WaitingFlip`, `Seeking`, `Settling`, and `Anchored`. Enabled construction allocates per-thread fingerprint and work baselines and reserves a reading trail; disabled construction does not allocate those vectors. The beat is `lb_tick_ms`, or `max(1, nthreads)` milliseconds if that knob is zero. During an issued flip it polls at `max(1, tick_ms / 8)` to measure transition cost (`src/core/flipctl.h:257`, `:291`, `src/core/flipctl.cc:230`, `:1297`, `src/core/server.h:410`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:286:`ThreadCtx` embeds a `FlipFingerprintWriter`: two plain cumulative/partial windows, a work-window value, and a pass countdown. With `flip_work_window = W` (default 100), the first parse pass is sampled and subsequent sampled passes are uniformly 1 through `2W-1` passes apart, using IO's xorshift draw. Every dispatched frame in a sampled pass contributes; unsampled passes only decrement the countdown. `W=1` is exhaustive. Zero disables the writer, and all fused boots configure it dark. A sampled pass adds seven command-class counts, total commands, multikey key/operation counts, non-key argument bytes, and one depth bucket (1, 2–4, 5–16, or over 16 frames), then increments `closed_windows` (`src/core/flipctl.h:22`, `:38`, `:65`, `src/core/io_loop.h:5311`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:288:The classification uses the registry's legacy first/last/step key range, not scatter's command-specific key oracle. “Value bytes” means **all non-key argument bytes**, including numeric/options/script arguments. `AtomicGrouped` wins for any multi-key `MultiShard` command when boot `cfg.atomic` is set, including multikey reads; it does not ask whether this operation actually admitted an atomic group. Fingerprint fields are plain owner stores and the monitor copies the struct without a release/acquire snapshot protocol; checking `closed_windows` after that copy does not produce an atomic window (`src/core/io_loop.h:5330`, `src/core/flipctl.cc:297`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:294:Pass-depth distance is retained for diagnostics and excluded from this trigger. The learned band is the maximum of twice pre-anchor jitter, `2/sqrt(max(sampled commands, 1))`, and the noise bound. A positive typed band substitutes its percentage for the first term, retaining the other floors; zero prevents mix triggering. The noise bound uses EW mean/variance and a decaying maximum, `max(peak, mean + 2*sqrt(variance))`, after at least two observations. Before anchoring it learns adjacent/learning-origin distance; afterwards it judges distance from the fixed anchor **first**, and learns only in-band observations (`src/core/flipctl.cc:51`, `:111`, `:153`, `src/core/flip_policy.h:287`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:296:Throughput is the delta of summed `ThreadCtx::total_commands_` divided by elapsed monitor milliseconds. Ordinary commands increment it on execution, scatter once at IO publication, and IO-local commands at IO execution; it is not a count of sent replies or executor fragments. A rate window resets if flip/LB is non-idle, snapshot/loading is active, or completed/refused flip and moved-client/shard counters changed. Otherwise every tick contributes to the long noise estimator. Its sample is the second relative difference `(r[t]-2*r[t-1]+r[t-2])/r[t-1]`; magnitude over 1 resets variance as a level change. Near-idle samples break the difference chain. EW time constant is `max(1, 30000/tick_ms)` ticks, with running-average warmup; reported sigma is RMS second difference, deliberately not divided by sqrt(6) (`src/core/thread.h:425`, `src/core/flipctl.cc:284`, `:339`, `src/core/flip_policy.h:247`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:298:A “stabilized” reading averages two adjacent tick rates when their relative distance, normalized by the larger magnitude, fits the typed/anchor/automatic band floored by twice long-window sigma. Automatic pair band is `2*max(pair distance, 1/rate)`. After acceptance, the second tick remains the first tick of the next pair: readings **overlap**. Anchored detection averages the pair without the stability rejection so a step can be detected. These are internal served-command observations; the controller cannot establish matched offered load (`src/core/flipctl.cc:334`, `:372`, `:395`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:302:Boot ignores rates at or below `nthreads * 1000/tick_ms` commands/s and resets its learning on such a tick. If fingerprinting is enabled, it also waits until at least one sampled work window appears. Non-idle deferral is capped at `ceil(30000/tick_ms)` ticks. Before that cap it uses a 0.5 rate EWMA, 0.5 EWMA of changes in normalized EWMA slope, and a five-position trend history. It starts when five-tick normalized slope is at most `2*max(slope-change jitter, (1000/tick_ms)/rate EWMA)/sqrt(5)` (`src/core/flipctl.cc:409`, `src/core/flipctl.h:521`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:304:At an anchor, mix shifts require consecutive out-of-band **sampled** observations; a tick without a fingerprint neither increments nor resets the streak. Rate surge/collapse requires consecutive pair means strictly above/below `anchor_rate * (1 +/- band)`. Both start with two confirmations. Pending rate evidence takes precedence over a simultaneous mix shift. In-band rate observations alone update anchor rate and jitter with alpha **1/64**; typed rate band stays typed, automatic rate band cannot fall below its settling floor. `flip_auto_band=0` disables these automatic change triggers, but does not disable the boot maneuver, forced trigger, controller vectors, or measurement machinery (`src/core/flipctl.cc:1221`, `:1272`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:306:Starting a maneuver records the current split, resets demand/origin/target windows and mix learning, and arms operation-age sampling at the explicit `lb_age_sample_rate`, or `nthreads` when it is zero. It sets the maximum model readings to `max(2, floor((30000/tick_ms)/2))`. That is a reading cap, not a wall-clock deadline; missing/unstable/transition-contaminated evidence can extend elapsed time indefinitely. Automatic mix/rate changes **cannot interrupt any active maneuver**. Only a forced trigger restarts it, waiting for an in-flight ownership transaction to finish first (`src/core/flipctl.cc:504`, `:1108`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:310:For every stabilized reading, the monitor measures each physical thread's `work = max(0, wall_ns - max(0, idle_delta))`. IO share `f` is total IO work divided by total IO+EX work; each role must have positive observed operations and work. Busy counters are not the denominator. Role headroom is the minimum `idle_delta/wall_ns` among that role's threads. Both roles' headroom greater than the current verification band causes `hold-unsaturated`; a forced seek bypasses it. Unbooked scheduler time is counted as work by this formula (`src/core/flipctl.cc:690`, `:806`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:312:The Welford demand window needs at least two samples. Its interval is mean `+/- 2*sample_sd/sqrt(n)`, clamped inside `(0,1)` with `1e-9` endpoints. With one role unit per thread, or per SMT sibling pair, it evaluates every legal `s = 1..N-1` using `R(s,f) = min(s/f, (N-s)/(1-f))`. The candidate maximizes gain over the live split at the mean. Its pessimistic gain is the minimum at interval low, mean, and high; the optimistic bound is the maximum any split reaches at those three points. Move requires pessimistic gain **strictly above** the bar; no candidate's optimistic gain above the bar yields a hold; otherwise sampling continues (`src/core/flip_policy.h:70`, `:109`, `:152`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:314:Verification band `B` is at least twice the origin reading range divided by its midpoint and twice long-window sigma. A typed percentage supplies another floor; auto also takes the previous anchor band and twice maximum observed pair jitter/one-command quantum. Required gain is `min(1, B * margin)`. The chooser's model-space bar is `min(1, required_gain/kappa)`; `kappa` starts at one and learns delivered/predicted gain magnitude. Noise-only refusal keeps sampling to the cap instead of immediately treating the current split as optimum (`src/core/flipctl.cc:740`, `:759`, `:857`).
ARCHITECTURE-CONTROLPLANE.md:320:A noiseless origin needs one; nonpositive denominator, fewer than two origin readings, nonpositive gain, or a result above the model reading cap means continue measuring origin, then hold at the cap. Predicted transfers are `clients * abs(io_after-io_before)/max(io_after,io_before)`, multiplied by the measured actual/naive transfer ratio. Measured transfer cost is total lost commands divided by clients moved; it is zero before the first measured move. The blackout is `(mean flip ticks + 3 + n_t - 1) * tick_seconds`. Flip duration has a one-tick floor even though its completion is polled eight times per tick (`src/core/flip_policy.h:325`, `:334`, `:392`, `src/core/flipctl.cc:831`).

Delivered gain strictly above it is a hit; strictly below its negative is an immediate miss; otherwise reaching the planned target-reading count is a miss. A miss issues a return to that hypothesis's departure split. A refused return or unexpected split falls back to the highest individual recorded rate in the trail, not to a fitted throughput curve (`src/core/flip_policy.h:353`, `:385`, `src/core/flipctl.cc:955`, `:980`).

A later miss returns to this landing, not necessarily to the maneuver's original split. Thus `Seeking` is neither an adjacent exhaustive sweep nor a single immutable jump.
